Illustrative example from the book: Meridian Industries

  • Closest archetype Meridian Industries: the hardest estate, with two legacy ERPs, a mainframe and 620 interfaces.
  • Invest first in Data readiness. A board that funds agents first and data second pays twice.
  • First three pilots Resolve AP price and quantity variance exceptions; Resolve customer billing disputes and credits; Answer how-to and policy questions at the service desk.
  • Top risk COR-01 migration larger than estimated.

Where to begin

Start from your role

Three steps for each reader. Each one opens a page on this site.

  • CEO or board

    1. Human-led, agent-operated
    2. How much should we fund?
    3. Who sets autonomy and who answers for it

  • CFO or finance

    1. Compare in cost per completed outcome
    2. How do we build the business case?
    3. Reimagined workflows

  • CIO or technology

    1. Reference architecture
    2. The harness, not the model, sets the ceiling
    3. Models in the solution framework

  • Risk or audit

    1. Controls library
    2. How do we manage risk, regulators and auditors?
    3. Decision trace viewer

  • Operations

    1. Reimagined workflows
    2. Design your own workflow
    3. Operating agents

  • Investor

    1. The value-risk flywheel
    2. How do we scale from pilot to portfolio?
    3. What’s inside the book

  • New to agents

    1. The autonomy scale, L0 to L5
    2. What’s inside the book
    3. Ask the book a question

The book

What’s inside the book

Share on LinkedIn: “Autonomy is earned when value compounds faster than risk.” (opens in a new tab)
  • The autonomy scale, L0 to L5. Evidence-based promotion and automatic demotion.
  • Guardrails. The controls every agent runs inside: identity, policy, limits, evaluation and the kill switch.
  • Domain chapters. Nine domains, from finance and procurement to legal, risk and insurance.
  • The case and the plan. Business-case models, operating-model changes, a 30-month roadmap and a risk register.
  • Meridian Industries. One fictional company runs through every chapter.
